records.title: Chromatin Remodeling of RasGRP3 Underlies Temozolomide Sensitivity in Glioblastoma Organoids.
records.abstract: Acquired resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) constitutes a formidable clinical barrier in the management of glioblastoma (GBM). GBM organoid models (GBO) that faithfully mirror the parental tumor phenotype serve as powerful research instruments to overcome the limitations in this field. We established GBOs derived from primary glioma patients and their TMZ low-sensitivity counterparts. To unravel the intricate molecular underpinnings of this process, we performed an unbiased, integrated multi-omics analysis encompassing epigenomic, 3D genomic, and transcriptomic profiling, coupled with dual CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screening of TMZ-induced enhancers (TiEns) and their cognate target genes. Our findings demonstrate that enhancer-mediated 3D chromatin remodeling drives chemosensitivity predominantly by transcriptionally activating drug-sensitivity-associated genes, such as RasGRP3, VEGFA, BTN3A2, etc. Knockdown or knockout of these genes and enhancers renders glioma cells more sensitive to TMZ, especially RasGRP3. Our work unveils a druggable "enhancer-chromatin-target" signaling axis and proposes a novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy to surmount TMZ low sensitivity in GBM.

records.title: An Intra-BET Epigenetic Mechanism Driven by BRD4 Controls Pancreatic α-Cell Expansion.
records.abstract: Pancreatic α cells play essential roles in maintaining glucose homeostasis. However, the epigenetic mechanisms governing α-cell proliferation and differentiation remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a systematic screen of a targeted PROTAC library and identified BET proteins as key regulators of α-cell proliferation and function. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that BRD4 promotes the acquisition of an intermediate endocrine progenitor-like state in progenitor cells. In vivo, α-cell-specific deletion of Brd4 markedly reduced α-cell mass and suppressed Men1-driven pathological α-cell proliferation, demonstrating that BRD4 is required for the establishment and/or maintenance of α-cell identity and abundance in vivo. Mechanistically, we identified the histone methyltransferase KMT5B as a BRD4-interacting protein and demonstrated that BRD4 directly binds to and represses the BRD2 promoter, with this BRD4-BRD2 regulation being modulated by KMT5B. Combined BRD4 overexpression and BRD2 suppression accelerated endocrine differentiation, reduced progenitor identity, enhanced α-cell features, and increased glucagon secretion in human islet organoids. Collectively, our study identifies a previously unrecognized KMT5B-modulated BRD4-BRD2 regulatory mechanism that coordinates pancreatic α-cell proliferation and differentiation, providing new insights into intra-BET epigenetic regulation during α-cell development and functional maturation.

records.title: [Resistance Mechanisms and Recent Advances in the Third-generation EGFR-TKI Osimertinib for Non-small Cell Lung Cancer].
records.abstract: Lung cancer is one of the malignant tumors with the highest morbidity and mortality worldwide, and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for approximately 85% of all lung cancer cases, with lung adenocarcinoma being the predominant histological subtype. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) sensitizing mutations are among the most common and important actionable driver alterations in Chinese patients with lung adenocarcinoma, and the advent of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) has inaugurated a new era of precision targeted therapy for lung adenocarcinoma. Osimertinib, a third-generation EGFR-TKI, has become the standard first-line treatment for advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC and substantially improves survival; however, acquired resistance remains the central limitation to long-term benefit. This review first delineates the distinction between primary and acquired resistance, then summarizes the principal mechanisms underlying acquired resistance to Osimertinib, including EGFR-dependent alterations, bypass pathway activation, histological transformation and cellular plasticity, tumour microenvironment remodelling and metabolic reprogramming, as well as recently identified mechanisms such as SWI/SNF-related, matrix-associated, actin-dependent regulator of chromatin, subfamily A, member 4 (SMARCA4) loss, the YAP1/AXL axis and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) epigenetic adaptation. Based on the frequent co-occurrence of multiple resistance mechanisms, we further summarize clinical-scenario-based therapeutic strategies and representative domestic and international studies after resistance to third-generation EGFR-TKIs, so as to provide theoretical references for overcoming Osimertinib resistance. Overall, precise resistance profiling via rebiopsy and liquid biopsy, rational pathway-directed combination therapy, and the integration of next-generation EGFR inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates and patient-derived organoid drug sensitivity testing are expected to transform EGFR-mutated NSCLC from inevitable resistance into a manageable chronic disease. .

records.title: Vascularized immunocompetent cortical organoids for modeling human brain development and disease.
records.abstract: Many current cortical organoid models lack key interacting cell types, including vascular and microglial cells, which are essential for brain tissue function and homeostasis. In this study, we have successfully developed an advanced organoid model through the incorporation of vascular and immune cells. These organoids exhibit capillary-like structures and microglial cells and show neuronal activity as revealed by calcium imaging. This cellular complexity was further confirmed by single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), which detected neurons, microglial cells, and vascular cells, recapitulating the developmental stage of the fetal transcriptome. In addition, electron microscopy revealed a putative capillary lumen surrounded by endothelial cells. Furthermore, transplantation of these organoids into the mouse brain showed human capillaries in close proximity to mouse capillaries. Taken together, we developed a vascularized, immunocompetent cortical organoid that may serve as a model for studying both neurodegenerative diseases and cerebrovascular dysfunction.

records.title: ID3 endowment and TGFBR2 deletion enhance iPSC-derived CAR macrophage immunotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma.
records.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies are limited by poor infiltration and immunosuppression in solid tumors. We developed induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived CAR macrophages (CAR-iMac) targeting glypican-3 (GPC3) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), incorporating ID3 endowment and TGFBR2 deletion. Single-cell RNA sequencing associated these modifications with enhanced inflammatory and phagocytic programs and reduced TGF-β responses. In orthotopic HCC preclinical models, magnetic particle imaging (MPI) of labeled CAR-iMac monitored in vivo distribution and persistence, together with histological phenotyping and transcriptional profiling, revealed dose-associated phenotypic state changes to guide dose optimization. The optimized regimen showed antitumor activity and preliminary safety in humanized mice. Additionally, CAR-iMac inhibited orthotopic patient-derived xenograft growth and cooperated with patient-matched T cells in patient-derived HCC organoids to enhance tumor killing and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. These findings supported a scalable macrophage platform integrating functional enhancement, longitudinal cell tracking, and rational dosing.

records.title: Malignant pleural effusion-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells promote lung cancer organoid proliferation via FGFR-MAPK/ERK pathway activation.
records.abstract: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is often associated with poor prognosis in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Previous studies have shown that regulatory B cells (Bregs) can suppress the anti-tumor immune response in MPE, but the potential role of Bregs in promoting lung cancer and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Pleural effusion-derived organoids were successfully established from three of four patients with NSCLC and characterized by HE staining and IHC analyses. These organoids were co-cultured with sorted CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells isolated from malignant pleural effusion (MPE) or paired peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) obtained from the same patients. The formation efficiency of organoids and their proliferation status were evaluated through microscopic observation and EdU labeling detection. Mechanism exploration was conducted using RNA sequencing. Additionally, A549 cells were co-cultured with MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells, and related signaling pathways were analyzed using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. The FGFR inhibitor (infigratinib) was applied to verify the involvement mechanism of the MAPK/ERK pathway. Compared with the control group, MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells significantly promoted the proliferation of pleural effusion-derived organoids. Transcriptomic analysis showed enrichment of the MAPK signaling pathway in organoids co-cultured with MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells. Consistently, in A549 cells, co-culture with MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells significantly increased the protein expression of VEGFA, FGFR1-3, and p-ERK1/2, while total ERK1/2 remained unchanged. FGFR inhibition attenuated Breg-like cell-associated proliferation and reduced ERK1/2 phosphorylation. These findings suggest that MPE-derived CD19+CD24+CD27+ Breg-like cells are associated with enhanced lung cancer organoid proliferation and activation of the FGFR-MAPK/ERK pathway, with p-ERK1/2 emerging as an important downstream readout associated with this response. The FGFR-MAPK/ERK axis may represent a potential therapeutic target in the context of MPE-associated lung cancer.

records.title: LeakageHunter-SCFM: Evidence-bounded dataset-lineage auditing for single-cell foundation model benchmarks.
records.abstract: To develop and evaluate LeakageHunter-SCFM, an evidence-bounded informatics framework for auditing dataset-lineage evidence and calibrating benchmark-independence claims in single-cell foundation model evaluation. LeakageHunter-SCFM extracts accessions, DOIs, URLs, and repository identifiers from manuscripts and related artifacts. The workflow canonicalizes resources, assigns dataset roles, constructs candidate overlap pairs, and applies claim ceilings before reviewer adjudication. We evaluated it in a curated development corpus, a locked retrospective external evaluation set, and a small prediction-blinded prospective proof-of-concept evaluation. The development workflow reduced 673 raw candidates to 84 filtered resource entries and 53 candidate overlap pairs. Prediction-visible reviewer forms agreed across all 140 retrospective evidence units; their historical labels yielded F1 0.842 across 132 binary-scored units. Independent prediction-blinded relabeling of all 140 units followed by third-assessor adjudication yielded precision 0.727, recall 0.667, specificity 0.910, and F1 0.696 across 136 binary-scored units. The seven-record, prediction-blinded proof of concept achieved recall 1.000 and precision 0.611 across 52 evidence units. All actionable-positive units came from one record. Restricting this analysis to full article bodies retained 50 units from five records and F1 0.759. Evidence-bounded lineage auditing supports biomedical foundation-model benchmark review by separating identifier overlap, actionable review priority, and confirmed exposure. LeakageHunter-SCFM provides a reproducible triage layer for lineage evidence and reserves claims about corpus membership and performance effects for direct supporting evidence.

records.title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
records.abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: scREFINE: Label-efficient refinement of frozen scGPT embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) clustering remains challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, technical noise, and limited cell annotations. Here, we propose scREFINE, a label-efficient semi-supervised clustering framework that adapts pretrained single-cell foundation-model embeddings for accurate cell clustering. scREFINE uses a lightweight refinement head to map cells into a task-specific clustering space using only 5% labeled cells, while treating the remaining cells as unlabeled during training. To exploit information from unlabeled cells, scREFINE introduces stability-aware soft structural regularization over local neighborhoods, which leverages reliable cell-cell relations as auxiliary guidance without relying on hard pseudo-label constraints. Experiments on five benchmark scRNA-seq datasets show that scREFINE achieves the best ARI on every dataset against every baseline under an identical, leakage-free protocol (mean ± SD over four seeds). A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the five per-dataset means yields p=0.0625, above the conventional 0.05 threshold because only five datasets are available; we therefore interpret the consistent improvements as strong empirical evidence rather than a statistically conclusive demonstration. A common-embedding comparison confirms that these gains arise from task-specific refinement rather than the pretrained representation alone: adapted baselines receiving identical embeddings achieve 0.00-0.61 ARI, compared with 0.73-0.89 for scREFINE. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that task-specific embedding refinement is the primary driver of improvement, whereas soft structural regularization provides dataset-dependent auxiliary gains and degrades more gracefully than hard pseudo-labels when supervision is scarce. Biological marker-gene analysis confirms that the predicted clusters correspond to canonical cell populations.

records.title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network.
records.abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: Reprogramming Protein Function by Expanding Chemical and Combinatorial Space: Integrating Chemical and Computational Strategies.
records.abstract: Proteins are biological macromolecules that perform critical functions, including catalysis, molecular recognition, and cellular regulation. Natural evolution has generated remarkable protein diversity, leaving vast opportunities for engineered molecular innovation. Protein engineering has evolved from the rational design of proteins over the last few decades to approaches based on directed evolution and computational methods to enhance their properties. Protein engineering is shifting from optimization-based approaches to an integrated approach, which includes rational design, directed evolution, computational and generative modeling, synthetic chemistry, synthetic biology, and laboratory automation. These strategies widen the scope of experimentally accessible chemical and structural toolboxes in proteins without sacrificing the physicochemical constraints, cellular compatibility, evolutionary processes, and experimental validation. Meanwhile, synthetic chemistry is extending the natural abilities of proteins by incorporating noncanonical amino acids, novel cofactors, and modified metal centers and catalytic environments. These technologies enable the creation of artificial enzymes, programmed molecular binders, synthetic receptors, molecular machines, and biomaterials that have functions beyond those of their natural counterparts. This review introduces advances in the protein engineering field, from past methods of modifying proteins to present-day opportunities for generating proteins with artificial intelligence, and explains how the fields of computation, chemistry, and biology are driving the future of programmable proteins.

records.title: Recent advances in fabrication strategies, functional modulation and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels.
records.abstract: Native protein-based hydrogels not only possess all advantages of their denatured analogues such as exceptional biocompatibility and low toxicity, but also retain the intrinsic function of the protein building block. Therefore, they exhibit novel favorable properties including inherent bioactivity and reversible sol-gel transformation behavior. As such, they have emerged as versatile biomaterials widely used in the biomedical field. This review provides a comprehensive and up-to date overview of design strategies, formation mechanisms, and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels. We systematically summarize the key cross-linking strategies for fabricating reversible native protein-based hydrogels, with particular emphasis on how these interactions govern hydrogel formation and their functionality. We highlight recent advances in fabricating these hydrogels through chemical cross-linking, physical cross-linking, metal coordination, fusion protein design, key interface redesign, de novo design, and modular design strategies, which enable precise control over hierarchical architecture, stimuli-responsiveness, and biomechanical properties. Furthermore, we explore the diverse healthcare applications of these hydrogels, with emphasis on drug delivery, wound healing, and tissue engineering. Finally, we discuss perspectives on future directions, including the integration of computational modeling, machine learning, and high-throughput experimentation to enable rational design of smart, multifunctional native protein-based hydrogels with tailored performances for next-generation biomedical applications.

records.title: Natural language-guided generation of molecular structures for single-molecule electronics.
records.abstract: As molecular science advances toward autonomous scientific discovery, enabling AI models to directly generate valid molecular structures from natural language descriptions has emerged as a critical requirement. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated the ability to map discrete chemical space into continuous semantic representation for general molecular generation, their application to single-molecule electronics (SME) remains largely unexplored. This is primarily due to the specific topological requirements of the field, such as the necessity of an anchor-backbone-anchor motif for electrode connection. In this work, we propose SingMolT5, a fine-tuned molecular LLM for natural language-guided generation of single molecules. We systematically evaluated the structural generation performance using both in-context learning (ICL) and fine-tuning strategies based on a carefully curated domain-specific instruction-tuning dataset. Results show that while ICL can capture basic molecular syntax, only the fine-tuning model can reliably enforce the anchor-backbone-anchor motif required for single-molecule measurements. More importantly, SingMolT5 achieved high structural prediction accuracy, along with strong generalization to unseen structural variations not included in the training dataset. This work provides a proof-of-concept demonstration for a text-to-structure workflow in SME, serving as a foundational step toward integrating natural language models into future autonomous workflows for single-molecule research.

records.title: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design.
records.abstract: Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

records.title: Genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity switches: Molecular design, pharmacology, and therapeutic considerations.
records.abstract: Genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity systems are chemogenetic tools that utilize small molecules to regulate protein association, higher-order assembly, and dissociation. Over the past three decades, an expanding repertoire of these systems has transformed the study of protein function and cellular signaling by enabling rapid, reversible, and tunable manipulation of protein localization, assembly, activity, and downstream physiological processes. As these technologies advance from experimental tools toward therapeutic applications, their translational potential depends not only on molecular switch performance but also on the properties of the chemical inducer and engineered protein components. In this review, we summarize the major classes and design principles of representative genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity systems, with particular emphasis on the pharmacological determinants that define their therapeutic operating window, including pharmacodynamic orthogonality, pharmacokinetics, tissue exposure, endogenous target engagement, and clinical readiness. We also examine how the biological origin and engineering of the chemogenetic modules influence immunogenicity and long-term compatibility. We further discuss exemplary applications, including pharmacological control of CAR-T cell activity, programmed cell death, CRISPR-based genome and epigenome engineering, and on-demand secretion of therapeutic proteins. Finally, we consider the delivery and coordinated expression of chemically regulated protein components as major remaining barriers to therapeutic implementation and highlight clinically compatible inducers, compact and minimally immunogenic protein modules, de novo protein design, and advances in viral and nonviral delivery as promising directions toward more reliable and pharmacologically tractable chemically controlled therapies.

records.title: Chemical Biology in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: From Ligand Discovery to Virtual Cells.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how scientists, including chemical biologists, conduct research. This review is intended to serve as an introduction for chemical biologists to applications of artificial intelligence in chemical biology. We review how chemical and biological data are featurized, the types of models commonly used in chemical biology applications, challenges in assessing accuracy of artificial intelligence models, and recent developments in agentic artificial intelligence for autonomous research. The applications we will cover include protein structure prediction, ligand discovery, peptide and protein design, prediction of mutational effects, interactomics and gene regulation, and virtual cells.

records.title: [From Immune Escape to Immune Remodeling: Mechanisms of Immunotherapy Resistance and Precision Intervention Strategies for Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer].
records.abstract: The application of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has substantially transformed the therapeutic landscape of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, primary and acquired resistance remain major barriers to achieving durable clinical benefits. Immune resistance is a dynamic and multifactorial process driven by tumor-intrinsic alterations, immune microenvironment remodeling, and dysregulated systemic immune responses. These mechanisms involve multiple layers of regulation, including neoantigen loss, impaired antigen presentation, dysregulated cyclic GMP-AMP synthase/stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS/STING) signaling, recruitment of immunosuppressive cells, metabolic reprogramming, CD8+ T-cell exhaustion, and disruption of intestinal and pulmonary microbiota homeostasis. This review systematically summarizes these resistance mechanisms and further outlines precision intervention strategies based on emerging ICIs, bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, adoptive cell therapies, tumor vaccines, and epigenetic or metabolic modulation. In addition, the potential value of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, tumor mutational burden, liquid biopsy markers, and multi-omics signatures for predicting therapeutic efficacy and monitoring resistance is discussed. In the future, precision treatment strategies integrating multidimensional biomarkers and comprehensive immuno-ecological analyses may enable dynamic prediction and effective reversal of immune resistance, thereby advancing personalized and adaptive treatment approaches for advanced NSCLC. .

records.title: [Research Advances in Exhaled Breath Condensate Multi-omics for the Diagnosis and Clinical Translation of Non-small Cell Lung Cancer].
records.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the predominant histological subtype of lung cancer and it is characterized by high incidence, insidious onset, and poor prognosis. Early diagnosis remains challenging, as low-dose spiral computed tomography (LDCT) screening has a high false-positive rate, highlighting the need for more specific adjunctive diagnostic approaches. As a lung-proximal, non-invasive liquid biopsy, exhaled breath condensate (EBC) can directly reflect alterations in the local airway microenvironment and is increasingly emerging as an important complement to conventional liquid biopsy approaches. In recent years, EBC research has evolved from single-omics biomarker screening toward integrated multi-omics analyses encompassing genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics. Meanwhile, the introduction of technologies such as microfluidics, nanosensing, and artificial intelligence algorithms has helped overcome key challenges associated with the high dilution of EBC samples and the trace abundance of target molecules. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in EBC research, including the standardization of sample collection, multi-omics biomarker discovery, innovations in detection technologies, and clinical translation. Particular emphasis is placed on the clinical value of EBC in the early screening, molecular subtyping, therapeutic response monitoring, and early warning of drug resistance in NSCLC. Current challenges and future directions are also discussed, with the aim of providing a reference for advancing EBC-based multi-omics technologies toward precision diagnosis and treatment in clinical practice. .

records.title: AI-assisted liquid biopsy for early breast cancer detection: a laboratory translation framework for future multimodal integration.
records.abstract: Early breast cancer detection is imaging-dependent in clinical laboratory medicine, and there are important limitations for interval cancers and women with dense breasts. Liquid biopsy is being developed as an adjunct to imaging and tissue diagnosis. There are two classes of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) features and a separate class of extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated biomarkers, such as microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and proteins, to consider in the proposed framework. These literature reviews primarily focus on combinations of individual modalities, cfDNA-only combinations, cfDNA-protein panels, and multicancer models. There is a lack of prospective clinical validation of a machine learning model that integrates all three modalities for the early detection of breast cancer. We categorized performance evidence based on the purpose of the test for average-risk screening, dense breast triage, symptomatic assessment, high-risk surveillance, recurrence monitoring for breast cancer, and metastatic disease detection, and differentiated between direct breast cancer evidence and indirect methodological analogies. Translation involves modality-specific specimen processing, modality-specific analytical and clinical validation, locked/version-controlled pipelines, patient-, site-, and time-level data partitioning, leakage control, pre-specified thresholds and abstention rules, calibration assessment, external validation, subgroup analyses, reportable quality-control metrics, and defined revalidation triggers.

records.title: Cell-free RNA signatures derived from the tumor microenvironment predict outcomes of CAR T therapy in large B cell lymphoma.
records.abstract: Anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy can induce durable remission in patients with large B cell lymphoma (LBCL), yet outcomes remain variable. Reliable pre-treatment predictors of durable response remain limited, leaving a critical gap in patient management. To address this, we profile pre-treatment plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA) from 91 LBCL patients treated with axicabtagene ciloleucel. We demonstrate that signatures of "lymph node-like" tumor microenvironments (TMEs), previously identified in tumor biopsies and shown to correlate with favorable outcomes, are elevated in the pre-treatment plasma cfRNA of responders, but not in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Using unbiased approaches, we identify additional cfRNA signatures associated with 1-year clinical outcomes that capture the underlying biological landscape of treatment response. Collectively, these findings support that pre-treatment plasma cfRNA could serve as a minimally invasive surrogate of TME state to potentially inform CAR T cell therapy outcomes and support risk stratification and TME-modulating adjunct therapies.

records.title: Plasma proteomics at the crossroads: Technological innovations driving clinical translation.
records.abstract: Proteomics has become an important tool in disease research by elucidating changes in protein expression and regulation under diverse pathophysiological conditions. Plasma, one of the most accessible biofluids for liquid biopsy, not only harbors an abundant proteomic repertoire but also provides a dynamic reflection of pathophysiological alterations. Consequently, plasma proteomics holds significant promise for translational research. However, challenges such as strong interference from high-abundance proteins in plasma, technical bottlenecks in detecting low-abundance functional proteins, and the complexity of post-translational modifications have substantially hindered the translation of plasma proteomics from basic research into clinical applications. Therefore, this review summarizes the latest breakthroughs in plasma proteomics methodologies, focusing on innovative advances across five core areas: sample preparation, separation technologies, integrated microfluidic platforms, detection technologies, and data-analysis workflows. Concurrently, it elaborates on the key application achievements and translational value of these technologies in three major clinical directions: real-time disease monitoring, early diagnosis, screening and risk stratification, and emerging applications, providing researchers in the field with a comprehensive technical reference and insights into clinical translation.

records.title: Navigating improvement activities in the diagnostic radiology MIPS value pathway: Practical guidance for radiology practices.
records.abstract: To provide radiology practices with practical guidance for selecting, implementing, documenting, and sustaining Improvement Activities (IAs) within the Diagnostic Radiology Value Pathway (MVP). CMS guidance, Diagnostic Radiology (DR) MVP requirements, and radiology-specific resources were reviewed by subject-matter experts to identify strategies that support meaningful participation in the IA performance category. Many CMS-approved IAs were originally designed for patient-facing specialties and are not readily applicable to diagnostic radiology. Numerous existing radiology initiatives, including peer learning, clinical decision support, structured reporting, dose optimization, quality collaboratives, registry participation, and communication programs, can be aligned with MVP requirements to better enable radiologist performance in the IA category. Successful participation depends on careful activity selection, integration into existing practice workflows, and maintenance of audit-ready documentation. Participation in the DR MVP is most effective when IA options are tailored to diagnostic radiology. Professional society resources, registries, and practice-level quality programs can reduce reporting burden while supporting meaningful improvements in quality and patient care.
